finding: Merged WP702 G4 blocks a direct forged constructor only when the caller omits its InitVar origin token. The origin token is the module-global _EVALUATOR_ORIGIN object, so a same-process caller can read that module attribute and pass it back to the public constructor. This is convention-level origin gating, not non-self-grantable producer lineage.
positive_evidence_preserved: G4 exact PR-head CI and existing OFF/taint/policy semantics remain valid at their bounded component scopes; the counterexample is specific to the stronger producer-lineage claim.
reproduction: Exact G4 source inspected plus standard-library dataclass/InitVar mechanism reproduction: dataclasses.replace without origin is rejected; explicit sentinel self-grant succeeds. Exact-source execution attempt in the analysis container was DNS-blocked and is not counted as product evidence.
successor: Prefer WP700 G2's already-admitted factory-only public-constructor-fails pattern for WP702, removing a caller-supplied origin authority argument. Add direct-constructor, dataclasses.replace, and no-caller-readable-constructor-capability falsifiers; require exact successor CI. Still do not claim hostile-same-process cryptographic security.
external_primary_support: PEP 8 explicitly treats underscore names as non-public conventions and states Python attributes are not truly private; SLSA/in-toto remain structural provenance references only, not dependencies for this repair.
handoff: Triggerword 4 should preserve G4 positive evidence, record the post-acceptance counterexample, avoid duplicate mutation if a successor claim already exists, and otherwise open the smallest successor producer-lineage generation using the WP700-style factory-only pattern.
